title: weak-signal-routing-pinboard
content:
Goal: collect quick thoughts and a rolling list of small experiments for routing low-confidence/weak-signal requests to appropriate fallbacks or specialized handlers. This is a lightweight pinboard — not a formal PRD yet.

Context + motivation:
- We get a small but nontrivial fraction of requests where model signals are ambiguous: short prompts, low-token-context, odd vocabulary, or high uncertainty in logits. Those requests cause either bad UX or expensive retries.
- Instead of monolithic fallback rules, can we surface a set of cheap, surface-level detectors + policy primitives that route to different lightweight handlers? Handlers can include: smaller cheaper model, template responder, clarification prompt, cached exemplar, or human review queue.

Hypotheses:
1) A small ensemble of cheap heuristics (token-length, OOV rate, confidence threshold, historical-user-clarity-score) will catch >70% of problematic requests early.
2) Routing to a templated clarification or compact model reduces average token-cost by ~30% while raising first-response accept rate.
3) Users tolerate short clarifications if they cut latency and deliver higher-quality results.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want a simple SDK hook that returns a routing decision (primary, fallback, clarify) plus metadata so I can instrument impact.
- As an SRE, I want the routing decision to be explainable (which detector fired) so we can audit and tune thresholds.
- As a customer success rep, I want to toggle the clarify-handler for a user cohort to test conversion impact.

Cheap detectors (first-pass ideas):
- length_short: prompt tokens < 6 -> higher ambiguity score
- token_entropy: cheap softmax proxy from small model -> if entropy high -> ambiguous
- exemplar-match: embed similarity against cached canonical prompts -> if low similarity -> new variant
- oov-rate: fraction of tokens not in model vocab/typo-heavy -> candidate clarify
- recency-signal: user has recent failed attempts for same intent -> escalate to human review

Handler ideas (ordered by cost):
- canned-template (fast, deterministic)
- micro-model (tiny quantized variant, 1-2 GPU/Tape-run, cheap)
- clarifying question (single-turn prompt that asks 1–2 quick Qs)
- cached exemplar reply (serve previously accepted answer for matched intent)
- human triage (slow, last resort)

Routing policy primitives:
- soft-priority scoring: detectors contribute weighted score -> threshold bins map to handlers
- per-customer knobs: prefer cheaper handlers for free-tier; prefer clarify for enterprise
- fallback chains: try micro-model -> if fails -> clarify -> if fails -> human queue
- latency SLO guardrails: if estimated handler time > SLO -> pick a cheaper handler or immediate degrade

Metrics to track (minimal):
- detection precision/recall (detector fired vs actual problematic request)
- cost delta per request (tokens, time) after routing change
- acceptance rate on first response (did the user accept or need retry?)
- clarify completion rate and conversion to successful answer
- human review rate and turnaround

Quick experiments (MVP cadence):
1) Logging-only rollout (2 weeks): add detectors to request path, log signals + gold outcome (user feedback/redo) to validate detectors.
2) Shadow routing (4 weeks): compute routing decisions but do not apply them; measure predicted improvements and false-positive rate.
3) Canary clarify-handler (2 weeks): for 5% of traffic, when detector triggers, interject a single clarifying question; instrument drop-off vs conversion.
4) Micro-model cheap-run (6 weeks): deploy tiny model for a subset of ambiguous requests; monitor cost and latency.

Risks / gotchas:
- Over-triggering clarifications -> user annoyance and retention hit. Need conservative thresholds and A/B tests.
- Complexity of per-customer knobs can become operational overhead. Prefer a small set of standard profiles.
- Metrics lag: hard to get a fast signal for correctness without high-quality user feedback. Build heuristics (follow-up edit, repeat queries) as proxies.

Implementation notes (initial):
- Prototype detectors as server-side fast functions implemented in Rust/Python inside request preprocessor. Keep dependency footprint minimal.
- Expose a simple routing API: decide(request) -> { decision: string, reasons: [string], score: float }
- Persist decisions & detectors outputs to telemetry pipeline for offline analysis (one row per request).
- Add UI toggles in Console for: enable/disable clarify, per-customer profile, threshold tuning.

Open questions / to-do (for next pass):
- What are cheap proxies for model uncertainty that scale? (temperature-based proxies, small proxy heads?)
- Should detectors be learned classifiers (tiny NN) or purely heuristic? tradeoffs: accuracy vs interpretability.
- UX for clarify: modal vs inline vs progressive hints — which has lower friction? need quick user research.
- How to tie detectors to model metadata: different models have different vocab and behaviors, detectors might need per-model calibration.

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- Talk to Mira + Sanjay to scope shadow-routing logging schema (who: Jordan, due: 2024-09-19).
- Hook a short-term telemetry flag to capture 'clarify-candidate' and 'detector-reasons' (owner: infra-eng contact: Sanjay).
- Draft a minimal Console toggle mock in Figma for clarify on/off (owner: product-designer TBD).

Notes to self / misc:
- Keep it cheap: focus on detectors with near-zero per-request extra tokens.
- Aim to be reversible: any routing change must be opt-out per-customer.
- Think about dataset drift: detectors tuned on current traffic may age; add periodic recalibration step.

End of pinboard — leave as evolving list. Will convert to a one-pager + experiment plan if signals look promising after shadow run.
